hypothesis: Compact content-addressed Hyperposition handles can reduce repeated semantic annotation transport, and sound factorization/distributivity can let a UnifiedDB preprocessor compute over unresolved alternatives without enumerating flat possible worlds.
interpretation: Experiment 1 supports only the engineering value of interning/references under repeated metadata; it does not show improved cognition.

Experiment 2 demonstrates the known distributive/factorization mechanism class on a deliberately factorable synthetic expression; it is not evidence that arbitrary Frank Hyperposition workloads admit this speedup.
The important architectural gate is law soundness: factorization/reuse is allowed only when the active carrier and material read/effect contracts license the rewrite.
counterhypothesis: The measured gains are entirely attributable to conventional content addressing and algebraic factorization; HyperMath adds no unique computational benefit unless real target traces show better semantic preservation, planning or cost than those baselines.
next_test: Current target-VPS Frank replay comparing plain ClayCode/UnifiedDB, conventional hyperrelation+factorized planner, and HyperMath law-carrying planner with identical state, model, seeds, effect policy and budgets.
